subject: Multi-cloud catalog harmonization: offer variants & co-sell gating
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sara Blake <sara.blake@aws-partners.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud catalog harmonization: initial proposal and asks

Team / Sara —

We need a short decision today on how we ship a harmonized offers catalog across AWS, Azure, and GCP for the upcoming co-sell push. Attached is a lightweight starting proposal (catalog-proposal.xlsx) and a token-level pricing matrix (pricing-matrix.csv). High-level goals:

- Keep parity in capabilities customers expect (hosted API, reserved/dedicated, private deployment)
- Minimize the number of offer variants per cloud to avoid co-sell fragmentation
- Ensure naming and SKU granularity align with each cloud’s co-sell/program requirements

Specific asks:
1) Can AWS accept a single "Base API" SaaS offer + a "Committed Capacity" reserved offer + a "Private" BYOL/managed option for co-sell eligibility?
2) What minimal metadata/plan-level fields do AWS/GCP need in our listing to enable co-sell (pricing tiers, region exposure, support bundle)?
3) Any hard constraints on regional availability (e.g., must list per-region or regional umbrella allowed)?

Jonas — please include partner enablement steps. Karthik — can you check Azure/GCP paralells and map owner for each cloud? Ben — I want a single-person owner for pricing updates.

If we can agree on the three canonical offer variants above, I think we can proceed with two CTA items: finalize canonical offer names + handoff to marketplace ops for listing builds.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Strategy, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: catalog-proposal.xlsx (xlsx), pricing-matrix.csv (csv)

From: Sara Blake <sara.blake@aws-partners.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud catalog harmonization: initial proposal and asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the files. Quick answers from the AWS catalog/co-sell side:

- AWS prefers a small set of offers for co-sell: a SaaS (metered) offer, a Reserved/Committed SKU (term-based), and a Marketplace listing for private deployments (often BYOL or private-lifted listing). Three variants aligns well with co-sell if the pricing/contracting model is clear.
- For co-sell eligibility you need: clear plan IDs, list price, USD per unit, region scope (global vs specific regions), support SLAs, and an AWS Partner Network (APN) listing ID.
- Regional nuance: AWS Marketplace supports both single-global listing with regional exposure and separate regional listings. For co-sell reporting we prefer a single offer with regional entitlements where possible — it makes revenue attribution simpler.
- Attach: aws-listing-checklist.pdf with our common gating items (legal, security artifacts, sample infra templates).

On private deployments: if you are offering an on-prem package, call it "Private (Managed/VPC)" and include a contact for contract provisioning — that speeds co-sell.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

— Sara
Sara Blake
AWS Marketplace Partner Manager
sara.blake@aws-partners.com

Attachments: aws-listing-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Sara Blake <sara.blake@aws-partners.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud catalog harmonization: initial proposal and asks

Marissa —

Thanks, read aws checklist. My recommend: canonical product family with three offer variants across clouds, but use cloud-specific plan IDs and naming conventions that map back to a single internal product code. Suggested external-facing names:

- Redwood API (Pay-as-you-go) — hosted SaaS meter
- Redwood Dedicated (Committed) — reserved/committed capacity
- Redwood Private (VPC / On-prem) — private deployment offering

Mapping notes:
- AWS: prefer single global offer + regional entitlements (per Sara). Use one plan ID per variant with term-based reserved SKU for Dedicated.
- Azure: marketplace prefers separate offer per pricing model in some cases; confirm with Azure PM but try to keep plan IDs mapped to our three canonical variants (we can alias names in Azure portal).
- GCP: requires containerized deployment artifacts for private/offline options; for SaaS we can register a single listing and expose region-level availability.

Risks: billing reconciliation if plan granularity differs per cloud. Mitigation: embed our internal product_code and hubspot deal id in listing metadata and ensure marketplace ops exports map to product_code.

Attaching the latest mapping doc: offer-mapping-v3.docx.

If there are no blockers from Azure/GCP owners by EOD, let's lock naming and I’ll push to marketplace ops.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud catalog harmonization: final decision and next steps

Team / Sara —

Summary and decisions (locked):
1) Canonical offer families (one internal product_code to rule them): Redwood API (PAYG), Redwood Dedicated (COMMIT), Redwood Private (PRIVATE). These will be the canonical map across AWS/Azure/GCP.
2) Cloud-specific constraints: AWS -> single global offer + regional entitlements where possible; Azure -> may require separate portal aliases but must map to internal product_code; GCP -> single listing for SaaS, additional container artifact for private option.
3) Co-sell gating: include plan IDs, list price in USD, support SLA field, product_code, and HubSpot deal id in listing metadata.

Owners and immediate next steps:
- Ben Carter: finalize pricing buckets and publish final pricing matrix (due Tue 2027-04-12).
- Karthik Iyer: own Azure and GCP listing intake, confirm any additional metadata by Mon 2027-04-12.
- Jonas Weber: open co-sell enablement ticket with AWS and schedule joint readiness call (target Wed 2027-04-14).
- Marketplace Ops: build listings once Ben/Karthik handoff complete.

Sara — appreciate the checklist. Can you confirm if APN ID assignment will take more than one week? If yes, flag and we'll adapt the go-live plan.

I'll create the confluence page and link to the handoff package.

Thanks all — tight timeline but achievable if owners hit the dates above.

Best,
Marissa

--
